comment_across_directive.c.reason: A block comment that spans lines ends the #define at the first newline, so X is 1 and '+ 2' leaks into the output.

if_character_constants.c.reason: The value of an ordinary character constant depends on the implementation's execution character set, so cpre declines to evaluate it instead of assuming ASCII.

linemodel_nel.c.cpre: rejected at line 1: ParseError: #if has no matching #endif
linemodel_nel.c.reason: Python's \s matches NEL (U+0085), so cpre treats '\u0085#if' as a directive; compilers treat it as ordinary text.

macro_stringify_indirect.c.reason: Stringifying an argument passed in by another macro drops the spaces between its tokens.

macro_va_opt_omitted.c.reason: C23 lets a variadic macro call omit the variadic argument entirely; cpre requires it, even if empty.

pragma_operator_indirect.c.reason: Same stringification bug: the _Pragma payload built through two macros loses its spaces.
